title: Thirteen Killed Including Infant as Landslide Crushes Taxi in Himachal Pradesh's Lahaul-Spiti
excerpt: The passengers had been stranded overnight after an earlier landslide blocked the road and were resuming their journey to Pangi Valley when boulders struck their vehicle.
body:
• At least 13 people, including a six-month-old infant, were killed when massive boulders from a landslide crushed a taxi on the Udaipur-Pangi road in Himachal Pradesh's Lahaul-Spiti district on Friday.
  • The 15 passengers had been stranded overnight after an earlier landslide blocked the road; they resumed their journey Friday morning when a fresh section of hillside gave way.
  • Only two survivors escaped by jumping clear before the vehicle caught fire after being struck.
  • Himachal Pradesh has been battered by continuous rainfall and landslides, with around 300 people dying annually from landslides across India.

At least 13 people were killed on Friday when a massive landslide sent boulders crashing onto a taxi carrying 15 passengers on the Udaipur-Pangi road in Himachal Pradesh's remote tribal district of Lahaul-Spiti, according to local authorities and news reports.

A six-month-old infant was among the dead. The SUV was completely crushed beyond recognition — its rear caved in by the impact — before catching fire. Only two passengers survived by leaping clear of the vehicle moments before it was engulfed in flames.

Stranded Overnight, Then Struck Again

The passengers had been stranded overnight at the village of Tindi after an earlier landslide on Thursday blocked the road. When the route was partially reopened Friday morning, they set off again toward Pangi Valley. Minutes into their journey, a fresh section of hillside gave way near Kadu Nala, sending debris cascading down onto the vehicle without warning.

The driver has been locally identified as Bir Singh. The remaining victims have not been formally identified. Army personnel and bystanders scrambled to the remote crash site to fight the flames, and relief teams have since reached the area to continue rescue operations.

Local authorities have ordered officials to personally oversee the rescue effort and instructed hospitals to provide the best possible treatment to the two survivors.

A Monsoon of Destruction

The tragedy is the latest in a series of devastating monsoon-related disasters to hit Himachal Pradesh this season. The Himalayan state has been battered by continuous heavy rainfall triggering landslides, flash floods, and road closures across multiple districts.

In a separate incident the same day, a woman was killed and seven others injured when a landslide struck their car as they travelled to a temple elsewhere in the state.

India loses an estimated 300 people to landslides annually, with the Himalayan states of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu & Kashmir among the most vulnerable. The combination of steep terrain, fragile geology, and increasingly intense monsoon rainfall — exacerbated by climate change — has made these disasters deadlier and more frequent.

A Warning for Travelers

Lahaul-Spiti and the surrounding Himalayan regions draw tens of thousands of tourists each summer, including many NRIs visiting India during the holiday season. Road conditions in these remote areas deteriorate sharply during the monsoon months of July through September, and landslides can strike without warning even on routes that have just been cleared.

State authorities and travel advisories have repeatedly urged caution on mountain roads during the monsoon season, though enforcement and early-warning infrastructure remain limited in many of the most vulnerable stretches.
nri_angle: Himachal Pradesh is a popular tourist destination for NRIs visiting India; the monsoon-season landslide toll raises questions about road safety in the Himalayas.
